body.text: Run start 2026-11-22T15:23:04Z, per status. Reconstruct both plug interactions from the full demonstration. Use the calibrated white plug geometry to link the hand and object tracks, then reserve the first delivery window for feasibility and the first gated neural policy.

body.summary: Full 436-frame two-adapter reconstruction in a shared metric scene with calibrated tabletop, moving camera, rigid adapter poses, and MANO right hand. The structural reference check is VALID. Physical checks expose contact and hand fit limits.

reprojection.note: against your own masks: agreement with them is necessary, not sufficient (3D errors along the viewing ray are invisible here)

anatomical_contact.note: a grasp needs the thumb and an opposing finger on opposite sides of the object; single-finger pushes or palm support are legitimate but must be stated in the analysis. Low penetration does not imply contact.

penetration_hand_object.note: unsigned (lower bound) distances where the object mesh is not watertight

self_penetration.note: triangle intersections between different fingers (FCL); counts are not volumes

physics.note: free-flight intervals are given with --flight OBJ=a:b; rest intervals default to object intervals without contact

handedness_scale.note: left/right are the demonstrator's anatomical hands; a hand is never mirrored

camera_focal.note: MoGe intrinsics are a learned prior; the focal should be calibrated against known geometry (camera_calib.py pnp). A large disagreement needs its explanation in NOTES.md (which one is wrong, and why).

body.text: r0002 exposed a monocular failure: the fitted thumb is 25–33 mm from the white adapter in the critical phases although the silhouette overlaps. I will test opposed distal finger contact and a distal collision term in a workspace copy of the fitter, and check whether they reduce the geometry errors without erasing the observed silhouette and finger motion.

body.text: The blade-axis change during the white turn stays above 42 degrees relative to the wrist across nearby phase endpoints in r0006. The black blade-tip labels reduce their reprojected RMS error from 43.8 to 15.3 px, but the resulting hand fit still intersects index and middle in 11 black-pickup frames. Repairing only that pair moved the collision to neighbors and worsened the fit. I am testing simultaneous constraints over all finger pairs in that short window.

body.summary: Whole-scene reconstruction passes the format and all geometric checks, with no right-finger intersections in 360 valid hand frames. The independently marked black blade tips reduce black prong RMS reprojection error from 43.8 to 15.3 px. Supplementary rigid support and hand–table checks pass.

body.text: Selected r0009 as the training reference. The reproduced MuJoCo bodies match the metric object tracks on all 436 frames, including the table. White moves 196.5 mm left in the demonstration. In the main turn the blade axis moves 42.6–58.8 degrees relative to the wrist across nearby boundary choices. I will use the lifted opposed turn, later transfer and supported release as the simulation skill. Occluded fingertip locations remain soft evidence for shaping.
